description.narrative: The Society of Women Graduates - SWG - The SWG project will focus on shelters located in marginalized areas across the Gaza Strip, where communities face extreme hardships due to prolonged war on Gaza, limited access to basic services, and deteriorating living conditions. These shelters are often underserved and lack the capacity to respond effectively to the needs of displaced populations. The project aims to improve the quality of services provided to IDPs while promoting the active participation of youth, especially young women, in community leadership and shelter management. SWG will provide capacity building programs on leadership, emergency response, and humanitarian principles for youth in shelters, particularly in Northern Gaza, awareness workshops for displaced women to encourage participation in shelter management committees and strengthen their leadership roles, the establishment of community participation committees comprised of trained youth and facilitation of stakeholder roundtable discussions, listening sessions with IDPs,and community dialogue events to ensure inclusive, needs-based shelter management and advocacy. The project ultimately seeks to empower youth from Northern Gaza to become influential community leaders, fostering more participatory governance within shelter settings.

participating-org.narrative:
The Society of Women Graduates in Gaza Strip (SWG) is a prominent non-governmental, non-profit organization dedicated to empoweringfemale university graduates in the Gaza Strip. Established in 1974, SWG focuses on enhancing the skills and capabilities of women graduates, enabling them to actively contribute to the development of the Palestinian community.
Mission and Objectives: Empowermentthrough Capacity Building: SWG offers development programs, skill rehabilitation, education, and awareness-raising initiatives to strengthen the competencies of women graduates.
Job Placement and Economic Integration: The organization assists in creating job opportunities for unemployed women graduates, facilitating their integration into the workforce.
FUND FOR INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT Advocacy and Rights Promotion: SWG advocates for the rights of women graduates by establishing local, regional, and international partnerships to support their cause.
Key Activities: Training Courses and Workshops: SWG conducts various training sessions and workshops aimed at enhancing the abilities of women graduates, preparing them for the job market.
Volunteer Programs: The organization encourages volunteerism among women graduates, promoting community service and engagement.
Life Skills Training: SWG implements life skills training to equip female university graduates with the necessary competencies to engage in professional and personal life effectively.
